Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Analyze the user's WES for a complete rare disease workup, including quality control, germline variant detection or processing, annotation, and candidate variant prioritization; clarify input formats and family structure. | rare-disease germline variant analysis of whole-exome sequencing, with input format to be confirmed → quality metrics and annotated candidate variants

Analyze the user's RNA-seq to support a complete rare disease workup, assessing disease-relevant expression and splicing abnormalities where supported; clarify bulk versus single-cell assay, input format, tissue, and reference cohort availability. | RNA-seq analysis for rare-disease transcriptomic evidence, with assay and input format to be confirmed → expression and splicing evidence supporting candidate disease genes and variants

Integrate WES variant findings with RNA-seq evidence for the user's complete rare disease workup, incorporating patient phenotypes and inheritance information once supplied to produce an evidence-ranked candidate report. | integration of annotated exome variants with transcriptomic expression and splicing evidence and phenotype-based prioritization → ranked candidate disease genes and variants with supporting evidence

Perform rare-disease analysis of whole-exome sequencing data: align or process exome reads, call and annotate germline variants, filter by inheritance and population frequency, and prioritize diagnostic variants. | rare-disease germline variant discovery from whole-exome sequencing reads or aligned exome data (quality control, variant calling, annotation, inheritance and frequency filtering) → prioritized annotated candidate variants

Perform RNA-seq functional analysis for rare-disease diagnosis, including expression outlier detection and aberrant splicing analysis to support candidate gene and variant interpretation. | rare-disease RNA-seq functional genomics analysis from RNA-seq reads or expression data (QC, alignment or quantification, expression-outlier and aberrant-splicing detection) → gene-level functional evidence supporting candidate variants

Integrate WES candidate variants with RNA-seq expression and splicing evidence to prioritize likely disease-causing genes and variants for a rare-disease diagnosis. | multimodal rare-disease diagnostic prioritization integrating annotated germline exome variants with RNA-seq expression-outlier and aberrant-splicing evidence → ranked candidate genes, variants, and supporting functional evidence

RNA-seq Differential Transcript Usage (rnaseqDTU). Bioc Workflow `rnaseqDTU` analog: quantify transcripts (Salmon), import via tximport, then + DEXSeq + stageR for differential transcript usage with FDR control.

Prepare the Bioconductor rnaseqDTU analogue, starting with Salmon transcript quantification of RNA-seq reads; input files and reference annotation remain to be supplied. | Salmon transcript-level quantification from RNA-seq reads using a reference transcriptome → per-sample transcript abundance estimates

Import Salmon transcript quantifications via tximport, preserving transcript-level information for the rnaseqDTU differential transcript usage analysis. | Import Salmon transcript quantification files with tximport for differential transcript usage → transcript-level counts and associated abundance and length information

Run DEXSeq-based differential transcript usage testing on tximport-derived transcript counts, using sample metadata, transcript-to-gene mappings, and contrasts to be supplied. | DEXSeq-based differential transcript usage testing on imported transcript-level RNA-seq counts with transcript-to-gene mappings and sample design → gene-level screening and transcript-level testing p-values

Apply stageR to DEXSeq differential transcript usage results for stage-wise false discovery rate control; the target FDR threshold remains unspecified. | Stage-wise multiple-testing adjustment with stageR on gene-level screening and transcript-level confirmation p-values → FDR-controlled differential transcript usage results

RNA-seq Differential Transcript Usage (rnaseqDTU). Bioc Workflow `rnaseqDTU` analog: quantify transcripts (Salmon), import via tximport, then + DEXSeq + stageR for differential transcript usage with FDR control.
Quantify RNA-seq transcripts with Salmon for the rnaseqDTU workflow. | Salmon transcript quantification from RNA-seq reads or alignments → per-sample transcript abundance and estimated count files

Import Salmon transcript quantifications with tximport for differential transcript usage analysis. | Import Salmon transcript quantification files with tximport using transcript-to-gene annotation → transcript-level abundance and count matrices

Test for differential transcript usage using DEXSeq on the imported transcript estimates. | DEXSeq differential transcript usage testing on imported transcript-level RNA-seq counts and sample metadata → transcript-level and gene-level statistical evidence

Apply stageR to the DEXSeq differential transcript usage results for stage-wise FDR control. | Stage-wise testing of gene-level and transcript-level differential transcript usage p-values with stageR → FDR-controlled transcript usage results

RNA-seq Differential Transcript Usage (rnaseqDTU). Bioc Workflow `rnaseqDTU` analog: quantify transcripts (Salmon), import via tximport, then + DEXSeq + stageR for differential transcript usage with FDR control.

Quantify transcript abundances from bulk RNA-seq reads using Salmon for a differential transcript usage workflow. | transcript-level quantification from bulk RNA-seq FASTQ reads using Salmon → per-sample transcript abundance and count estimates

Import Salmon transcript quantifications with tximport and prepare transcript/exon-level count data for DEXSeq differential transcript usage testing. | import Salmon transcript quantifications with tximport and construct DEXSeq-compatible transcript/exon usage count objects → normalized count data and experimental design inputs

Perform differential transcript usage testing with DEXSeq on the imported RNA-seq transcript-level counts. | differential transcript/exon usage testing on DEXSeq-compatible bulk RNA-seq count data → gene- and feature-level usage statistics, effect sizes, and p-values

Apply stageR to DEXSeq differential transcript usage results for stage-wise FDR control and final significant transcript-usage calls. | stage-wise false-discovery-rate control on differential transcript usage results using stageR → FDR-controlled significant genes and transcript/exon usage features

ATAC-seq accessible chromatin region calling | open chromatin peak calling from ATAC-seq reads (Tn5 transposase insertion data), with peak-level accessibility quantification → accessible region set with signal and significance

ChIP-seq transcription factor binding peak calling | transcription factor binding peak calling from ChIP-seq reads against an input control, narrow-peak mode → binding sites with fold enrichment and significance

Link ATAC-seq accessible regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks to differentially expressed genes | integration of differential gene expression results with accessible-chromatin regions and TF binding peaks, linking peaks to nearest or regulatory-domain target genes by genomic proximity → gene-level regulatory evidence table with peak-gene links

Assign CRISPR guides to cells in a Perturb-seq screen, using Replogle et al. 2022 as the methodological reference. | Assign CRISPR guide identities to individual cells from Perturb-seq guide-capture data and associate them with single-cell expression profiles → cell-level guide assignments and quality metrics.

Call CRISPR perturbation hits using the guide-assigned Perturb-seq cells, guided by Replogle et al. 2022. | Perform perturbation hit calling on guide-assigned single-cell expression data using suitable controls and statistical testing → ranked perturbation effects and significance estimates.

Characterize perturbation states using scVI and scANVI embeddings of the Perturb-seq data and called hits, guided by Replogle et al. 2022. | Model perturbation states in guide-annotated single-cell expression data using scVI and scANVI embeddings → latent representations and visualizations annotated by perturbation and hit status.

Perturb-seq guide assignment: assign sgRNA identities to single cells in the pooled CRISPR screen (reference: Replogle JM et al. 2022 Cell, doi:10.1016/j.cell.2022.05.013) | guide-to-cell assignment for pooled CRISPR perturbation single-cell RNA-seq: demultiplex sgRNA feature counts per cell, threshold and assign a dominant perturbation identity per cell → per-cell guide assignment table with assignment confidence and cell-level perturbation labels

Perturb-seq hit calling: identify perturbations with significant transcriptional effects relative to controls | differential expression of each perturbation versus non-targeting control cells on single-cell count data (pseudobulk or per-cell test) with multiple-testing correction → per-perturbation hit calls with effect sizes and adjusted p-values

Perturbation state embedding with scVI / scANVI on the Perturb-seq cells | deep generative latent embedding of perturbed single-cell RNA-seq counts with scVI or scANVI, conditioned on perturbation labels and batch covariates → per-cell latent embedding, perturbation-state scores, and UMAP visualization

Prepare the guide-assignment stage of an end-to-end Perturb-seq CRISPR screen pipeline, using Replogle JM et al., Cell 2022, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2022.05.013 as the methods reference. Obtain the user's input format and files before execution. | guide assignment for a single-cell Perturb-seq CRISPR screen using guide-capture reads or a processed cell-by-guide count matrix, with input format to be confirmed → cell-level guide assignments and assignment quality-control metrics

Perform Perturb-seq CRISPR screen hit calling after guide assignment, using the single-cell expression data and assigned perturbations. Derive the appropriate statistical approach and controls from Replogle JM et al. 2022 and confirm required parameters with the user. | perturbation hit calling in a single-cell CRISPR screen from a gene-expression count matrix and cell-level guide assignments → perturbation-effect statistics, multiple-testing-adjusted significance, and screen hits

Analyze perturbation-associated cell states and generate scVI/scANVI embeddings as the final stage of the Perturb-seq pipeline, incorporating upstream guide assignments and hit-calling results. Use Replogle JM et al. 2022 as the reference while distinguishing the requested embedding tools from methods actually reported in the paper. | latent embedding and perturbation-associated cell-state analysis of single-cell CRISPR screen expression counts with guide assignments and hit annotations using scVI and, when suitable labels are available, scANVI → cell embeddings and perturbation-state summaries

Guide assignment for a Perturb-seq CRISPR screen, following the Replogle et al. 2022 Cell approach: assign sgRNAs to cells from single-cell guide-capture data and filter cells by assignment confidence. | sgRNA-to-cell assignment for a pooled single-cell CRISPR screen (Perturb-seq) from guide-capture and gene-expression single-cell data, with cell QC and filtering of multiplets and unassigned cells → per-cell guide/perturbation identity table and filtered cell-by-gene count object

Hit calling for the Perturb-seq screen: identify perturbations with significant transcriptional effects relative to non-targeting control cells. | hit calling in a Perturb-seq screen by testing each perturbation against non-targeting control cells (differential expression and/or energy-distance / transcriptome-wide effect tests with multiple-testing correction) → per-perturbation effect size, significance and on-target knockdown table

Perturbation state analysis using scVI / scANVI latent embeddings of the Perturb-seq cells. | latent-space embedding of single-cell Perturb-seq data with scVI / scANVI (batch-aware variational autoencoder, label transfer with perturbation labels), followed by UMAP and clustering → per-cell latent embedding, perturbation-state clusters and perturbation-level summaries

Step 1: Guide assignment in Perturb-seq CRISPR screen single-cell data | sgRNA guide barcode calling and assignment to single cells from Perturb-seq sequencing reads or CRISPR feature barcode count matrix → cell-to-guide assignment table and filtered single-cell object

Step 2: Hit calling on guide-assigned Perturb-seq single-cell data | perturbation hit calling and differential expression testing across CRISPR perturbations vs non-targeting controls in single-cell Perturb-seq data → significant gene perturbations and transcriptional effect sizes

Step 3: Perturbation state modeling and latent embedding using scVI / scANVI | variational autoencoder latent representation and perturbation state embedding of single-cell Perturb-seq transcriptomes using scVI and scANVI → latent embedding coordinates, perturbation state clusters, and annotated AnnData

Implement the Replogle et al. (2022) Perturb-seq guide-assignment stage: process single-cell CRISPR perturbation sequencing inputs to assign guide RNAs/perturbations to cells and generate an annotated cell-by-guide matrix. | Perturb-seq CRISPR guide assignment from single-cell RNA-seq and guide-capture sequencing data → cell barcode–guide assignments, guide UMI counts, multiplet/low-confidence assignment flags, and an annotated single-cell expression object

Perform Perturb-seq hit calling on guide-assigned single-cell data, identifying perturbations with significant molecular or phenotypic effects relative to appropriate non-targeting controls. | Statistical hit calling for a guide-assigned Perturb-seq single-cell dataset → gene/guide perturbation effect sizes, significance statistics, false-discovery-adjusted hits, and ranked perturbation candidates

Model Perturb-seq perturbation states using scVI/scANVI: learn a batch-aware latent embedding, annotate or transfer cell states where a reference is available, and quantify perturbation-associated shifts in latent state. | scVI/scANVI variational latent-state modeling of guide-assigned Perturb-seq single-cell expression data → batch-corrected embedding, reference-informed cell-state labels where applicable, perturbation-state coordinates, and visualization-ready UMAP

Perturbation state embedding using scVI / scANVI | single-cell representation learning and embedding using scVI/scANVI on perturbed scRNA-seq data → latent space embeddings

Identify tumor-reactive T cells in the user's scRNA-seq data | tumor-reactive T cell identification from tumor-infiltrating single-cell RNA-seq: T cell clustering and annotation, scoring of tumor-reactivity/exhaustion signatures (e.g. PDCD1, CXCL13, ENTPD1, HAVCR2), optional TCR clonotype expansion → ranked tumor-reactive T cell clusters and cell-level scores

Predict neoantigens | neoantigen prediction from tumor somatic mutations: variant-derived mutant peptide generation, patient HLA typing, MHC class I/II binding affinity and presentation prediction (e.g. pVACtools/NetMHCpan) → ranked candidate neoantigens

Identify tumor-reactive T cells in my scRNA-seq data | single-cell RNA-seq T cell analysis: T cell subset annotation, clonotype/TCR-based expansion scoring, and activation/exhaustion signature scoring on a processed single-cell count matrix or AnnData object → per-cell tumor-reactivity scores and reactive T cell cluster assignments

Predict neoantigens from my tumor variant data | neoantigen prediction from somatic tumor variants: somatic variant annotation, mutant peptide generation (8-11mers), HLA class I binding affinity prediction against the patient HLA genotype, and agretopicity/foreignness filtering → ranked candidate neoantigen peptides

Identify and characterize tumor-reactive T-cell populations in the user's scRNA-seq dataset, including T-cell clustering, annotation, activation/exhaustion markers, and tumor-reactivity signatures. | single-cell RNA-seq T-cell subset analysis and tumor-reactive T-cell identification from processed single-cell expression data or raw scRNA-seq reads → annotated T-cell clusters, tumor-reactivity/exhaustion scores, marker genes, and visualizations

Predict patient-specific tumor neoantigens from tumor somatic variants, RNA expression, and HLA genotype, prioritizing mutant peptides with predicted MHC binding and expression support. | tumor neoantigen prediction using somatic tumor variants plus HLA typing and optional tumor RNA expression → candidate mutant peptides ranked by predicted MHC binding affinity, expression, and clonality

Find tumor-reactive T cells in scRNA-seq data | identification and scoring of tumor-reactive T cell clonotypes and gene expression signatures from single-cell RNA-seq / scTCR-seq data → annotated tumor-reactive T cell populations and TCR clonotypes

Predict neoantigens matching the tumor and T-cell context | somatic mutation-derived neoantigen and MHC binding prediction from tumor variants / expression and HLA alleles → ranked candidate neoantigen peptides

IDAT → Normalisation → Differential Methylation → Gene Enrichment. EPIC/450K array methylation from IDAT — minfi load + functional normalisation, DSS differential methylation, missMethyl gene-set enrichment. Use when you want the DSS-based differential-methylation + enrichment wrapper chain. Also applicable to bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq.

Load EPIC or 450K methylation array IDAT files with minfi and perform functional normalization. | Load Illumina EPIC or 450K methylation array IDAT files with minfi and perform functional normalization → normalized methylation measurements and probe metadata.

Perform DSS-based differential methylation on the normalized array data; alternatively support Bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq when supplied. | DSS differential methylation testing using compatible normalized array measurements or Bismark bisulfite coverage → differential methylation results for downstream enrichment.

Perform missMethyl gene-set enrichment on the differential methylation results. | Gene-set enrichment with missMethyl using differential methylation results and compatible probe annotation → enriched gene sets and significance statistics.

Load EPIC/450K IDAT files with minfi and apply functional normalisation | Illumina EPIC/450K methylation array preprocessing from raw IDAT files: minfi loading and functional normalisation (funnorm) with QC, producing normalised beta/M-value matrices

Differential methylation analysis with DSS on the normalised methylation data | Differential methylation testing with DSS on a normalised methylation beta-value matrix, two-group comparison, giving differentially methylated CpGs/regions with effect sizes and adjusted p-values

Gene-set enrichment of differentially methylated CpGs with missMethyl | Gene-set enrichment of differentially methylated CpGs/regions with missMethyl, correcting for the number of probes per gene on the array (GO/KEGG), giving enriched gene sets with adjusted p-values

Load EPIC/450K methylation-array IDAT files with minfi and perform functional normalisation as the first stage of the DSS-based differential-methylation and enrichment chain. | Import EPIC/450K methylation-array IDAT files with minfi and apply functional normalisation → normalised methylation measurements and probe annotations for downstream differential testing

Perform DSS-based differential methylation after minfi functional normalisation of EPIC/450K IDAT data. Validate the wrapper's array-to-DSS input contract; alternatively, support Bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq. | DSS differential methylation testing using upstream normalised array methylation measurements only if the wrapper supports their input contract, or alternatively Bismark methylated/total coverage counts → differential methylation statistics and supported region-level results

Run missMethyl gene-set enrichment on the differential methylation results from the DSS-based EPIC/450K wrapper chain, validating annotation and background compatibility if using the alternative Bismark coverage route. | missMethyl gene-set enrichment from differential methylation results with tested CpG background and appropriate gene annotations → enriched gene sets and multiple-testing-adjusted significance
